attributes.summary:
Harvest round. The Contract Lifecycle Desk spec was built out overnight and this crawl is the first to see it: **25 of 25 of that spec's New and Extend rows now carry a Spec**, up from 13 yesterday. 17 rows were stamped, 14 of them newly verified.

What landed: the whole signature ceremony the spec designed and nothing had implemented — Signature Block, Signature Block View, Legal Party Role, Verify Signature — plus Clause Reference, Effective Period, Governing Law and Generate Document, and Specs for the four Extend rows (Clause, Signatory, Contract Status, Contract Execution App) whose code already existed.

Two review notes from yesterday were answered rather than ignored. **Effective Period did not fork Contract's term fields**: Contract keeps its flat startDate/endDate/autoRenews/renewalNoticeDays and gains `effectivePeriod` as an additive field, with the computed notice getters preferring it when set — a migration, not a parallel model. And **Legal Home now ranks by days-to-notice**, falling back to expiry, which was the one real defect in the earlier build.

Off-matrix inventory 114 -> 115 blocks; the gap profile is unchanged (2 no example, both blocked on primitive fields; 2 no consumer; 10 no call site; 30 single-consumer).

**New breakage this round, not from the crawl.** Three instances now fail to index: two Payment instances and Spec/payment-terms-field, all reporting an undefined card class. Cause is an import cycle — `payment-terms-field.gts` reads the value export `PaymentMethodField` from `payment.gts`, and `payment.gts` and `invoice.gts` import each other, so the enum is undefined when `PaymentTermsField.method` is declared. Both sides of the cycle were edited overnight. It needs the owner's call: move the enum to its own module, as `payment-status-field.gts` already is, or take the field type through a thunk.

Also unchanged and worth restating: gold is flat at 63 because the crawl still stamps no consumers, so every newly verified row lands Adequate.
